newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Madagascar votes for its next president.
newsitem.headline: Madagascar votes for its next president.

text.p: Voters in Madagascar went to the polls on Sunday with former Marxist military ruler Didier Ratsiraka expected to defeat his rival for the presidency, former president Albert Zafy.

It was the second round of voting following an election campaign that aroused little excitement in the Indian Ocean island republic. The second round was forced when none of the 15 candidates in the first round in November obtained the required 50 percent of votes cast.
There were no queues when polling stations in Antananarivo opened at 0600 local (0300 gmt), and electoral officials said they had no problems in coping with the turn-out.
Sale of alcohol was banned throughout Madagascar for the day and a team of observers from Francophone African countries was deployed to monitor the polls.
Polling stations were due to close at 1800 local (1500 gmt), but full results were not expected for several days.

Ratsiraka, 60, was widely tipped to win the run-off. He led the first-round poll with 36.61 percent of votes, against 23.39 per cent for Zafy, 69 -- whose impeachment by parliament in July forced the election.
Ratsiraka returned from 19 months of voluntary exile in France at the end of September to seek the presidency, and his level of support surprised many observers.

But diplomats said many people were disillusioned with the squabbling that had marked Zafy's rule since 1993. They said life in the former French colony had not improved and the islanders remain among the poorest people in the world.
